issue_context.title: Fix qwikswitch tests that have uncaught exceptions
issue_context.body:
We have just merged #33312 which makes sure that a test fails if it has uncaught exceptions while it was running. This was not considered a failure before.

We had to ignore several existing tests that had uncaught exceptions. This included some tests of the qwikswitch integration. These tests will need to be fixed.

The ignored tests can be found [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/ignore_uncaught_exceptions.py). To fix this, remove the lines for your integration from that file, run your test suite and make sure all tests pass.

review_comments:
Seems fragile to modify the constant. I'd copy it first unless there's some specific reason to do this.

Or wrap the object in a pytest fixture so we can get a new instance when needed, for each test or for the test session etc.

I agree that this test is designed in a way that was very confusing to me because of this.
However, I didn't want to rewrite the entire test for a component that I am not the expert on, so I used the same design pattern.
In the original version, in the first command that is sent, the command is sent followed by a ClientError. In the next one it wasn't and there was an exception because the list was read past its end, which caused an assertion. All I did was to append the same ClientError on the subsequent commands as well.
I definitely agree that the test could be refactored in a much more readable and maintainable way, and I can take it as a separate task. For example, I couldn't find examples of how to properly inherit from list and I am sure there is a more simple design. However, no reason to keep it always asserting on the loop, which is what i changed in this PR

BTW, it is not really a constant but used here as a global variable...
I can certainly take the task of refactoring it to something that even I can understand :)

We don't allow globals and if it's not a constant we should change the test.

I think returning the instance from a fixture would be an easy solution.

It's ok to do in a follow up.

trying to rewrite it since it seems weird to me. However, facing challenges, as it is not my code.

however, the globals are already in the code base. Hopefully will figure out how to get them out.

Is there someone who "owns" this code?

ok. in any case, i am trying to refactor it as an exercise for myself.
